question: When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, one of the alternate interior angles is 115°. What is the measure of the angle that lies opposite to it on the alternate interior side?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the basic geometric properties of parallel lines intersected by a transversal:

Alternate interior angles are always equal to each other.

Since one alternate interior angle is given as 115°, the angle opposite to it on the alternate side must also be identical.

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal
